title: Countable fundamental systems of open ideals descend along a taut map
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: In the situation of the taut descent statements of the chapter, the lemma asserts that if the target ring has a countable fundamental system of open ideals then so does the source (statement lines 1800-1805). The proof fixes such a system in the target and, using tautness, chooses for each member an open ideal of the source whose extension is contained in it; it then shows that these ideals form a fundamental system of the source (proof lines 1807-1811). For an arbitrary open ideal of the source it argues as follows: tautness makes the closure of the extension of that ideal open, so it contains one of the members of the target's system, whence the corresponding chosen ideal of the source has extension inside the extension of the arbitrary one; since the map between the corresponding quotients is faithfully flat, hence injective, and the composite of the map from the source to the chosen quotient with the map to the arbitrary quotient is zero, the chosen ideal is contained in the arbitrary one (proof lines 1811-1818). The claim is H2: the construction of the candidate system is followed by a genuine argument for it, in which faithful flatness of the map between the quotients is used to descend a vanishing to the source.
